title: Reduced-belt transient mechanics: final closure
scientific_question: Which surviving reduced-belt transient terms are important across Baja operation, high/asymmetric contact, mixed slip, overrun, and the vanishing-belt-inertia limit, and which coherent simplifications are justified?
analysis_lenses: ratio and belt-speed coverage through disturbance timing
high-contact stick and mixed-slip branch search
controlled true-overrun verification by boundary power sign
final-equation activity thresholds distinct from gross-force thresholds

baja_envelope.negative_grade_semantics: downhill/unloading under the normal full-throttle engine boundary; not asserted closed-throttle overrun

decision_gate: Call discovery complete when mixed/high-contact behavior has been exercised or its absence documented, true overrun has been verified, and the inertia continuations show whether the force-small whole-belt term is trajectory-small without materially changing hybrid events.

final_closure.overrun_semantics: controlled primary resisting torque plus downhill road; synthesis verifies actual power-flow reversal
